_about: What the port draws for what no level pictures - the portals a shot opens, the shot,
the player, and chapter 1's boss with its spikes - as the original's own entities draw
them. Their images are read from the extracted APK beside the remake and never
Each carries its .ent's <EmissiveColor>, because the original dims every sprite it draws
to min(1, ambient + emissive) of its colour (ETHRenderEntity.cpp:113-117), these as much
And each carries its .ent's lighting facts (step 49, the lighting design's G5): static and
applyLight, which decide which 2D lights reach it (Lighting::ReceiverMask); its <Normal>, a
file under the original's entities/normalmaps/, when it names one; and its <Light>, when it
has one, with the z the light's height is measured from.

_source: A LEVEL PROPERTY rather than an entity. Game's level-properties reader does
CheckCustomData('darkest') and, when it is set, SetAmbientLight(DARKEST_AMBIENT_LIGHT)
- and that single call is the whole of what the flag does in that function.
_moved: The ambient light itself, (0.01, 0.01, 0.01), now lives in lighting.json as
darkest_ambient, where the port's lighting reads it (step 45). The flag is carried on
Game::Level, and the layer multiplies every level sprite by min(1, ambient + emissive)
with that ambient in place of the file's.
Its ONE decoded gameplay consequence is not drawing at all:
canSeeAnything = GetAmbientLight() != DARKEST_AMBIENT_LIGHT, so a minion in a darkest
level is BLIND. minions.json records minion sight as not built. Lighting::Ambient is the
number sight must compare when it lands.

_initial_direction: (bytes 119493..119839) instructions 39-41 set direction = 2, MOVING_RIGHT. The row a character
stands on IS its direction: SideScrollerCharacter::updateFrame (bytes 130241..130614) instructions
88-102, every update with no walk, SetFrame(idleColumn, findFinalDirection(direction)), which is
row 2 column 0, frame 8, facing right. dark_mage.ent's startFrame 4 is not what shows:
replaced by the first update, and Ethanon's .ent reader has no startFrame read at all
(ETHEntityProperties.cpp reads type, static, shape, blendMode at :228-236; the clone names
startFrame only in its editor). MEASURED: the original stands on frame 8 in all 54 lit levels
where the player is located (the remake's visuals/briefs/systems_3_4.md 3a).

_note: Which row of the sheet walks which way: derived, not testimony. The original's
DIRECTION enum decodes to MOVING_DOWN 0, MOVING_LEFT 1, MOVING_RIGHT 2, MOVING_UP 3
(the remake's tools/asbc), and Ethanon's own sample picks a character's row by its
direction and its column by a frame timer (Sample-project/main.angelscript:102). The
sheet's row 1 faces left and row 2 right. The owner confirmed on 11 September that the
character turns as it walks; not which rows do it. DECODED since: updateFrame calls
SetFrame(column, findFinalDirection(direction)), and no FlipX or SetFlipX is called anywhere
in the bytecode, so walking left is row 1 unflipped. Rows 0 and 3, arm out, are the pushing

_source: DECODED (the remake's out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt, md5 48fe65ce). THE ROW:
SideScrollerCharacter::findFinalDirection (bytes 131207..131341) instructions 3-19 return
`pushing ? (direction == 1 ? 0 : 3) : direction` (the 1, MOVING_LEFT, is the CMPIu immediate
read as its vK operand, INFERRED as every such immediate is): pushing left draws row 0, pushing
any other way row 3 (the sheet's rows 0 and 3 hold the arm out left and right). Walking or
standing alike: updateFrame (bytes 130241..130614) passes it the direction at 63-67 and 89-93.
THE LAG: SideScrollerCharacter::update (bytes 153242..153396) calls updateFrame (instruction
18) BEFORE applyForces (29), which calls detectPushing (applyForces, bytes 129676..130142,
instruction 96): an update draws the push the update before found, so the first update
against a wall draws the walk and the update a walk stops on still draws the push.
THE RAY: detectPushing (bytes 130614..131207): when dirVec.x == 0, pushing = false (3-6,
108-111); else a ray from getPosXY() to getPosXY() + normalize(dirVec) x 0.6 x getSize().x +
vector2(0, scale(-6)) (8-52; the arguments pushed last-first put the -6 on y, 6 above, and
scale() makes it 6 level units, not screen pixels), and pushing = GetClosestContact(from, to,
point, normal, 'dark_mage.ent') != null (59-106). getSize() is ETHEntity::GetSize, the
sprite's frame size times the entity's scale (ETHSpriteEntity::GetCurrentSize,
ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:652-682): 0.6 x 40 = 24 units at the player's getScale(). dirVec is the
velocity applyForces has just set (instructions 38-56 and 86-91): x = moveVec.x x speedScale,
the walk, y = the body's vertical velocity; and where isTouchingGround is not set (63-84),
x = the body's own x velocity x min(1, GetFPSRate() / 60 x 0.86), 0.86 at the port's fixed
60 Hz tick (air_velocity_share). GetClosestContact(a, b, point, normal, ignore)
(ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:251-268) ignores entities by name alone (ETHEntityNameArrayChooser,
ETHEntityChooser.cpp:49-63) and keeps every other fixture the ray reports
(ETHRayCastCallback.cpp:40-51), sensors included: Box2D's world ray cast has no sensor test
(b2World.cpp:978-995) and a sensor entity has fixtures (ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:109). A
fixture the ray starts inside is not reported (b2PolygonShape.cpp:189-258, b2CircleShape.cpp:
47-82). NEVER WHERE GRAVITY IS OFF: MainCharacter::MainCharacter (bytes 126650..127790)
instructions 10-17 and 35 pass noGravity as SideScrollerCharacter's forceNoImpulse, whose
constructor (bytes 152667..153096) sets pushing = false (73-75) and keeps the flag (77-78),
and update skips applyForces while it is set (20-29): pushing never changes there.
MEASURED: no clip was taken for it (plan F11), but footage F9's take r6 (3-18) holds the right
pad into the corridor wall and draws row 3 at the wall and row 2 after the release, and F13's
fall (1-06, pad held) draws row 2 on every frame of the fall (planning doc step 64).
DECODED: SideScrollerCharacter::SideScrollerCharacter instructions 9-11 set frameStride = 90
(ms), and instructions 80-82 idleColumn = 0. updateFrame instructions 63-86, every update
with a walk, SetFrame(timer.set(0, 3, frameStride, true), findFinalDirection(direction)); with
none (88-102), SetFrame(idleColumn, ...) and the timer is not called. FrameTimer::set (bytes
23254..23650) adds the frame's elapsed ms (instructions 6-11), resets to `first` with no time
only when first or last differ from the last call's (13-44; the first walk's, against the
constructor's 0 and 0, bytes 22535..22652), else steps ONE column once the time reaches the
stride and takes the stride off (45-76). first and last are always 0 and 3, so the column
and its time carry across a stop and a turn, and on a level with gravity a stop adds no time.
Not called while paused or finished: MainCharacter::update (bytes 128578..128850) 6-21. The
loading screen's character keeps the same 90 ms (ui.json character.stride_ms). On the 18
no_gravity levels the same timer also turns while the player stands: no_gravity_motion.
MEASURED: 0.369 s a cycle of four, 92 ms a column, over 7 cycles of rec11 walking right
(the remake's specs/visuals/scripted.md section 1.4).

_source: DECODED: on a no_gravity level MainCharacter::update (bytes 128578..128850) calls
MainCharacter::linearMotion (bytes 132139..132833) after SideScrollerCharacter::update
(instructions 57, 66), on every update that is neither paused nor finished (6-21).
COLUMN: linearMotion instructions 163-174 call the character's FrameTimer as
set(0, 3, 280, true) and write the column into idleColumn, walking or not. FrameTimer::set
(bytes 23254..23650): the last frame's elapsed ms added (6-11); a reset to `first` with no time
when first or last differ from the last call's (13-44), so the first update resets it against
the constructor's 0 and 0; else one column once the time reaches the stride, the stride taken
off (45-76). updateFrame, which runs first, stands the player on idleColumn (88-102): the column
an update draws is the one the update before left. A walking update also calls set(0, 3, 90,
true) (63-86) and draws that, so it adds its time to the timer twice.
HOVER: linearMotion instructions 8-57, on the first call, set linearMotionAngle = PI + PIb
(hover_start_radians) and keep the pivot as originalPivotAdjust; 59-78 add unitsPerSecond(3), 3 rad
a second of frame time (STimeManager::unitsPerSecond, bytes 8045..8162, min(200, elapsed ms)
/ 1000 x the time factor); 92-112 take PI * 2 off once past it (hover_wrap_radians); 114-161
SetPivotAdjust(originalPivotAdjust + vector2(0, cos(angle) * 1.2)). GetPivotAdjust returns the
stored pivot times the entity's scale and SetPivotAdjust divides by it (ETHEntity.cpp:1019-1026),
and the draw multiplies by it again (ETHEntity.cpp:296): the 1.2 is added in SCREEN pixels, not
scaled with the level (the player is added at getScale(), GameCharacter::GameCharacter
instructions 10-24, screen height / 256). A larger pivot y draws the image higher (the origin
moves down it). A period of 2 PI / 3 = 2.094 s. The port's tick is a fixed 1/60 s, below the
200 ms cap.
PORT DECISION (P2 pattern, as ui.json's credits strip): 1.2 screen px is 0.4267 units only on a
720 px screen (1.2 x 256 / 720), so the port adds hover_screen_px x 256 / hover_at_screen_px
units at every window. R12 fixes the texture tier only. The original's is 1.2 x 256 / the
screen's height (0.64 units at 480 px, 0.28 at 1080 px): left for the owner (planning step 63).
The original's beholder.ent: Sprite beholder.png, blendMode 0, SpriteCut 2 x 1. Frame
0 has its eye open and frame 1 shut: ETHCallback_beholder sets 1 while it throws rocks
and 0 otherwise. Its CustomData scale, 0.75, is applied when it appears and replaced
on its first turn: bounce() (utilEntityEffect.angelscript) calls SetScale, which sets
the scale outright (ETHEntity.cpp:601). So it is drawn at its frame's size times its
pulse. The pulse goes from one scale to the other and back by smoothEnd, each way a
stride. While it throws rocks it keeps the last. Its colour is (1, hp / 2, hp / 2).
The original's beholder_spike.ent: Sprite beholder_spike.png, blendMode 0, SpriteCut
1 x 1, PivotAdjust (0, 10). Its image points down, and projectileBehaviour turns it to
where it flies: SetAngle(radianToDegree(getAngle(direction))).
A PLACED entity the level pictures, but drawn as its script redraws it: ETHCallback_portal_static
(Portal.angelscript, bytecode bytes 360571..361404, the remake's out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt).
Once, guarded by the uint 'scaled' (ops 1-12, JNZ -> 80 once it is set, ops 17-29 set it):
ops 14-16  thisEntity.Scale(0.8f). ETHEntity::Scale(float) scales the entity AND every particle
system it carries (ETHEntity.cpp:591-599 -> ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:512-518 ->
ETHParticleManager.cpp:444-451, ETHParticleSystem.cpp:27-40, PARTICLE::Scale
ETHParticleManager.h:160-164). The picture is drawn at its frame size times the
scale (ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:652-682): portal_halo.png 64 -> 51.2 u, the rings 110 -> 88.
ops 31-79  SetColor(GetString('color') == 'red' ? vector3(1, 0.3, 0.3) : vector3(0.3, 0.3, 1)).
An AngelScript call pushes its last argument first (the order systems_3_4 read
_portalColorA by, which footage confirmed), so ops 57-59 push z 0.3, y 0.3, x 1: red.
0.3f is PshC4 1050253722 (0x3E99999A). SetColor writes m_v4Color (ETHEntity.cpp:493-498),
which multiplies the SPRITE's min(1, ambient + emissive) (ETHRenderEntity.cpp:113-117);
a particle is drawn in its own colour times ambient alone (ETHParticleManager.cpp:381-389),
so the rings and the iris are not tinted.
A static entity with a callback runs it on every frame its bucket is drawn
(ETHScene.cpp:572 and 488, ETHActiveEntityHandler.cpp:70-74, 90-93 and 145-166), after its particles update.
Footage agrees on the order: red portals read pinker, R/B 0.82 against blue's 0.52 (scripted.md 2.3).
static_portal._not_applied: Scale also scales the entity's collision box (m_controller->Scale). The port's static portal is entered by its trigger_size box, which is gameplay, and is left as it was.
